elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (i): "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" — the per-occurrence floor is stated as a minimum, not a cap.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same clause (i) expressly sets "USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" as a "not less than" floor.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (ii): "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000."

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (iii): "cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering its processing of Credit Data and other Client data." The condition is engaged (TrueLink hosts the Web Site and transmits/archives borrower Credit Data) and the obligation is stated unconditionally, so it applies in all events.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Clause (iv): "workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law."

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "TrueLink shall provide Client with certificates of insurance upon request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (ii) requires E&O of "not less than USD 2,000,000," which exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (iii) requires cyber/privacy cover of "not less than USD 5,000,000," which exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: Finding kind "missing" is corroborated: the cited original text (Section 12(b) indemnity and the Section 12 liability cap) contains no insurance covenant, and the rationale records that a full-text search for "insur" surfaces only the recital reference to third-party mortgage insurers.

All six preferred elements are carried in a single inserted operative paragraph with express "not less than" floors, so the preferred level is position-complete; the fallback floors are satisfied a fortiori by the higher preferred limits.

Nothing is left to the margin comment: the comment merely explains the insertion and offers the fallback, while every limit, the workers' compensation covenant and the certificates undertaking appear in the operative text.

Minimal: the insertion is a single short paragraph tracking the playbook model language, adds no audit, additional-insured, waiver-of-subrogation, notice-of-cancellation or primary/non-contributory requirement beyond the checklist, and deletes nothing. The one-year tail after the term mirrors the model language and is not an extraneous addition.

Preserves intent: Section 12(b)'s indemnity and the all-caps liability cap for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 are reproduced verbatim and unaltered; the insurance covenant is an independent covenant that neither expands nor contradicts the existing allocation, remedies or fee mechanics.

Drafting nit only (not an element defect and not grounds to withhold completion): the inserted paragraph is headed "Insurance." without a subsection letter, whereas the surrounding Section 12 uses lettered subsections and the rationale describes it as Section 12(c) — conform the enumeration to "c." on execution. Consider also whether an insurance covenant is better sited in the miscellaneous sections than inside the indemnity section, though placement does not affect enforceability here.
